concept.technique_name: cube surface area to side to volume

examples.problem_statement: A perfect cube has surface area 96. What is its volume?

solution.description: Write the cube's surface area as 6 times the area of one face, since all six faces of a cube are identical squares.
Set the surface-area formula equal to the given 96 and divide both sides by 6 to isolate the squared side.
Take the square root of 16 to get the edge length of the cube.
Cube the edge length just found, because the volume of a cube is the side raised to the third power.

key_reminders: Surface area of a cube = 6(side)^2, since all faces are congruent squares.
Solve for the side first; it is the bridge between surface area and volume.
common_mistakes: Dividing 96 by 6 and stopping at 16, reporting the face area instead of taking its square root to get the side 4.
Cubing the surface area or the face area rather than the edge length of 4.

examples.problem_statement: Tae Yang has a stack of $20 bills totaling $1,600 and a stack of $10 bills totaling $1,050. (Assume that all bills have the same thickness.) Quantity A: The percent by which the height of the stack of $10 bills is greater than that of the stack of $20 bills. Quantity B: 33.5%. (A) Quantity A is greater. (B) Quantity B is greater. (C) The two quantities are equal. (D) The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

solution.result: comparing heights reduces to comparing bill counts
solution.description: Note that all bills have the same thickness, so the percent difference in stack height equals the percent difference in the number of bills.
Divide the $1,600 total by the $20 denomination to count the bills in the taller-denomination stack.
Divide the $1,050 total by the $10 denomination to count the bills in the other stack.
Plug the two counts into the percent change formula, using the $20 stack as the base since Quantity A asks how much greater the $10 stack is than it.

solution.result: Quantity A is less than Quantity B
solution.description: Convert the decimal to a percent and compare it with Quantity B, which is the larger of the two.

key_reminders: Equal-thickness bills mean stack height is proportional to bill count, not to dollar value.
Percent change = (new - original) / original, with the quantity being compared against as the base.
Convert the decimal result to a percent before comparing it with a percent quantity.
common_mistakes: Comparing the dollar totals 1,600 and 1,050 directly, since the larger dollar total belongs to the shorter stack.
Dividing by 105 instead of 80, which uses the $10 stack as the base rather than the $20 stack named in Quantity A.
Reading 0.3125 as 3.125% or 0.3125% instead of 31.25%, which flips the comparison against 33.5%.

examples.problem_statement: Freud's structural model of the psyche should be understood as (i) _________ device, useful for inciting and guiding discovery, rather than as an attempt to (ii) _________ physical relationships among parts of the human brain. Blank (i): a heuristic / a hermeneutic / an allegorical. Blank (ii): dictate / ameliorate / represent.

solution.operation: isolate the appositive defining blank (i): "device, useful for inciting and guiding discovery"
solution.result: blank (i) needs a word meaning "aiding discovery"
solution.description: Notice that the sentence itself defines the first blank, so read the phrase that follows it as the definition the answer must match.

solution.operation: match "useful for inciting and guiding discovery" to the blank (i) choices
solution.description: Select the choice whose meaning is precisely that definition; heuristic means exactly a device that aids discovery.

solution.operation: read "rather than as an attempt to (ii) ___ physical relationships"
solution.result: blank (ii) needs a word meaning "show" or "depict"
solution.description: Use the contrast: the model is not to be taken as a guide to the brain's physical structure, so the second blank must be a verb about depicting those relationships.

solution.operation: match "show" or "depict" to the blank (ii) choices
solution.description: Pick the choice closest to that meaning; represent is the nearest of dictate, ameliorate, and represent.

key_reminders: When a sentence supplies its own definition of a blank, the answer is the word that definition names.
"Rather than" signals a contrast, so build the second blank from what the model is being denied.
Predict a plain-English word before looking at the choices, then take the closest match.
common_mistakes: Choosing hermeneutic for blank (i) because it also sounds scholarly, though it concerns interpretation rather than aiding discovery.
Choosing dictate for blank (ii), which asserts control over the brain's structure rather than depicting it.
